quotes: "We present MatplotAlt, an open-source Python package for easily adding alternative text to Matplotlib figures." (p. 1)
"We describe the algorithms, templates, and libraries we use to automatically generate and surface alt text for Matplotlib figures." (p. 4)
"We evaluate MatplotAlt’s alt text generation methods on the VisText and Matplotlib gallery datasets." (p. 6)

entries.value: programmatically generated notebook figures commonly lacked alt text, leaving BVI users without a description (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "Notably, in their analysis of 100,000 notebooks, Potluri and Singanamalla et al. found that 99.81% of programmatically generated images did not have associated alternative text [PSTM23], which is a critical accessibility barrier [EBM22, C∗ 08]." (p. 2)

quotes: "These functions allow users to easily replace calls to matplotlib.pyplot.show with show_with_alt to generate accessible figure outputs." (p. 5)

rq3_entries.value: MatplotAlt parses chart features, creates a semantic-level heuristic or VLM description, and then embeds or exports it (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "Heuristic-based alt text of a given semantic level is generated from Matplotlib figure attributes using the generate_alt_text function." (p. 3)
"Alternatively, VLM-based descriptions can be generated with the figure as input using generate_api_alt_text." (p. 3)
"Descriptions are then embedded in the notebook or exported using add_alt_text." (p. 3)

rq3_entries.value: the author checks factual correctness, adds context and insight, and chooses how to present the resulting text (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "They check for factual correctness and manually add their own context and insights to the returned string." (p. 2)
"Finally, Rory displays their customized alt text with add_alt_text for Aida to review." (p. 2)

rq3_entries.value: author_raised — the authors warn that erroneous descriptions can mislead BVI users (PDF p. 10).
quotes: "At the same time, MatplotAlt’s current description generation methods are error-prone and could be misleading when used by BVI notebook users, as seen in our evaluation of description correctness (§5.5)." (p. 10)

rq3_entries.value: no — detail remains explicitly user-selected rather than decreasing with competence (PDF p. 4).
quotes: "Users can specify the amount of detail to include in alt text through the desc_level parameter, based on L1-L3 semantic levels [LS21]:" (p. 4)

rq3_entries.value: the person must verify factual correctness and supply context; the paper reports no reduction in this responsibility as expertise grows (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "They check for factual correctness and manually add their own context and insights to the returned string." (p. 2)

rq3_entries.value: not_applicable — the paper reports offline description evaluations rather than observation of people using the support.

claim_entries.value: the authors claim that the system generates effective Matplotlib alt text and that heuristic text and tables improve VLM factuality (PDF p. 10).
quotes: "Our initial qualitative evaluations indicate that MatplotAlt can generate effective alt text for Matplotlib figures, and that heuristic alt text and data tables can be used to increase the factuality of VLM descriptions." (p. 10)

claim_entries.value: working_system_evaluated — the implemented generation methods are evaluated on two datasets (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "We evaluate MatplotAlt’s alt text generation methods on the VisText and Matplotlib gallery datasets." (p. 6)

claim_entries.value: Mirri et al.’s CSV-to-XML graphics, Sharif et al.’s jQuery summarizer, and BrailleR’s templated descriptions and interactive SVG exploration (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "Mirri et al. explore using CSV content to create screen reader compatible XML graphics including basic alt information [MPS∗ 17], and Sharif et al. develop a jQuery plugin which summarizes HTML/Json figure types, values, and basic statistics [SF18]." (p. 3)

"Allowing a range of exploration methods, BrailleR [GWS∗ 24] supports both creating templated textual descriptions of graphs in R and exploring different chart features with a screen reader in an interactive SVG." (p. 3)

claim_entries.value: description length, similarity to reference captions, image–text similarity, qualitative error types, and error frequency across generation methods (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "We quantitatively measure description length (§5.1), similarity to reference VisText captions (§5.2), and similarity between image and alt text embeddings (§5.3)." (p. 6)
"Next, we qualitatively categorize types of errors in MatplotAlt’s descriptions (§5.4) and compare their frequency in different generation methods (§5.5)." (p. 6)
"We present MatplotAlt, an open-source Python package for easily adding alternative text to Matplotlib figures." (p. 1)

claim_entries.value: the offline comparisons support relative factuality and similarity claims, but “effective” user-facing alt text is broader than the evidence because the authors cannot establish a generally good default and report substantial quality variation (PDF p. 10).
quotes: "Our evaluations of alt text generations may not be perceived as rigorous as they do not offer definitive guidelines of specific generation strategies of MatplotAlt as good defaults." (p. 10)

"Given the variability in alternative text quality across different measures as shown in our evaluations, and varying preferences of BVI users on alt text [SKZ∗ 24], providing definitive defaults that work for all contexts is not feasible." (p. 10)

paper_code_entries.value: accessible computational-notebook visualization and alt-text authoring (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "We present MatplotAlt, an open-source Python package for easily adding alternative text to Matplotlib figures." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: both — the support is presented for learning new concepts and for immediate data exploration (PDF p. 10).
quotes: "Using these tools, BVI experts can perceive notebook visualizations that they may encounter in the wild to learn new concepts or conduct data exploration." (p. 10)

paper_code_entries.value: mixed_or_transitioning — the scenarios include a working developer and a student learning a package (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "Aida is a BVI developer in a data analysis team comprised of BVI and sighted scientists." (p. 2)
"Dez is a BVI student trying to learn a new Python package by reading its documentation page." (p. 2)

paper_code_entries.value: execution_or_skill_gap — inaccessible notebook infrastructure prevents BVI users from perceiving figures and gives authors no native way to attach descriptive text (PDF p. 2).
quotes: "Despite their ubiquity, notebooks remain inaccessible to blind and visually impaired (BVI) users due to the authoring practices, tools, and infrastructures used in their creation and sharing [PSTM23]." (p. 2)
"Additionally, no popular computational notebook software currently supports the addition of descriptive text to displayed images." (p. 2)

paper_code_entries.value: artifact — the evaluation measures generated descriptions rather than user process or learning (PDF p. 6).
quotes: "We quantitatively measure description length (§5.1), similarity to reference VisText captions (§5.2), and similarity between image and alt text embeddings (§5.3)." (p. 6)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — semantic levels organize description content from encodings through broader context (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "Different levels include information about encodings and axes (level 1), relevant statistics (level 2), trends (level 3), and broader context about the chart (level 4)." (p. 3)

paper_code_entries.value: hybrid_or_multi_model — VLM prompts can incorporate deterministic heuristic text, chart tables, or both (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "To capture both perceptual phenomena (e.g. overlapping points, color patterns) in images and semantic relationships between figure elements, we add chart data to prompts by including either a markdown data table (VLM + table), the heuristic-based alt text for the chart (VLM + heuristic), or both (VLM + table + heuristic)." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: llm_era — GPT4-turbo generates one of the scaffold’s meaning-bearing description paths (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "We find that state-of-the-art LLMs still struggle with factual errors when describing charts, and improve the accuracy of our descriptions by prompting GPT4-turbo with heuristic-based alt text or data tables parsed from the Matplotlib figure." (p. 1)

limitations: "One downside of this approach is that it assumes all charts have a single type." (p. 4)
"For example, our current system cannot correctly classify overlaid bar and line plots in the same figure." (p. 4)
"Our system also currently fails on interactive and dynamically updated charts." (p. 4)
"Unlike heuristic alt text, we note that there is no guarantee VLM descriptions will adhere to semantic guidelines." (p. 5)
"Alternative text and figure descriptions alone, however, do not support the full extent of data exploration needs of BVI experts [SCWR21, SWM∗ 22]." (p. 10)
"Our evaluations of alt text generations may not be perceived as rigorous as they do not offer definitive guidelines of specific generation strategies of MatplotAlt as good defaults." (p. 10)

"Although the desc_level parameter allows users to modify the inclusion of information, we leave it to feature work to support changing the verbosity and ordering of generated descriptions, which are also important modes of customization for BVI users [JPPH∗ 24]." (p. 10)
"Additionally, our generation strategies may not be effective for several chart types or plotting methods used by Matplotlib users as our evaluations used carefully curated images." (p. 10)

"The alttextify command begins to make the infrastructure to run such at-scale evaluations available, but still requires executing arbitrary code, which is potentially dangerous in untrusted notebooks." (p. 10)
boundary_conditions: "Extending previous work [KLL∗ 22, TBS23] that focus on only the one to three most popular chart types, MatplotAlt currently supports ten types of figures: line, bar, scatter, radial line, pie, strip, contour, heatmap, image, and boxplot." (p. 4)

"For high-stakes analysis in the medical domain, for example, MatplotAlt’s dry but interpretable templated descriptions are likely more appropriate [Rud19] compared to those generated by a VLM that potentially contain errors and hallucinations." (p. 4)
"Descriptions for personal learning on well-documented problems, however, may benefit from the adaptability and extra context provided by VLMs [RNK∗ 23]." (p. 4)
